explanations.4: This line lists which tools you're allowed to use — the asterisks mean you can run any bash command that starts with those names (like `ls` or `find`), plus one specific script for getting the next ID.
explanations.11: The 'todo-authoring' skill is a separate set of rules that defines what things like 'Depends' mean in a todo file; you might need to load it if you're unsure about the format.
explanations.19: A 'slug' is a URL-friendly version of the title: all lowercase, only letters and numbers and dashes, no extra words like 'the' at the start.
explanations.31: This script looks at every todo file in `.todos/` (even ones in subfolders) and finds the highest ID number already used, then adds 1 to create the next one.
explanations.33: NNNN means a 4-digit number with leading zeros if needed, like 0042 instead of 42.
explanations.38: The filename format NNNN-slug is fixed and permanent — don't put status or priority in the filename because those change over time but the ID should never change.
explanations.59: These header bullets (Priority, Batch, etc.) are the specific lines that the `/todo-plan` command reads and parses to understand the task's metadata.
